item.title: Iran sentences Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi to 7 more years in prison
item.description: DUBAI, United Arab Emirates — Iran sentenced Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi to over seven more years in prison after she began a hunger strike, supporters said Sunday, as Tehran cracks down on all dissent following nationwide protests and the deaths of thousands at the hands of security forces.

item.title: U.S. gives Ukraine, Russia a June deadline to reach deal to end war
item.description: KYIV, Ukraine — The U.S. has given Ukraine and Russia a June deadline to reach a deal to end the nearly four‑year war, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told reporters, as Russian strikes on energy infrastructure forced nuclear power plants to cut output on Saturday.

item.title: Gaza’s Rafah crossing opens after two-day closure
item.description: CAIRO — A limited number of Palestinians traveled between Gaza and Egypt on Sunday as the Rafah crossing reopened after a two-day closure, Egyptian state media reported.

item.title: Court affirms policy of jailing immigrants without bond
item.description: President Donald Trump’s administration can continue to detain immigrants without bond, marking a major legal victory for the federal immigration agenda and countering a slew of recent lower court decisions across the country that argued the practice is illegal.

item.title: Government must reach agreement on right to counsel
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS — Attorneys for the federal government have until Thursday to reach an agreement with human rights lawyers who are seeking to ensure the right to counsel for people detained at an Immigration and Customs Enforcement facility in Minnesota, a judge said Friday.

item.title: Winter Olympics: Breezy Johnson, Ilia Malinin star for U.S. at Milan Cortina Olympics
item.description: MILAN — The crash. The gasps. The helicopter. Lindsey Vonn’s frightening fall in the women’s downhill at the Milan Cortina Olympics couldn’t help but overshadow U.S. teammate Breezy Johnson’s feat — winning her country’s first gold medal at these Games. item.title: SUPER BOWL CHAMPS: Seahawks use their ‘Dark Side’ defense to pound Patriots 29-13
item.description: Devon Witherspoon, Derick Hall, Byron Murphy and the rest of Mike Macdonald’s ferocious unit pummeled Drake Maye in Seattle's 29-13 win on Sunday at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif.

item.title: Super Bowl Key Play: Derick Hall’s strip-sack opens the way to Seahawks’ second title
item.description: The Seahawks had throttled the New England Patriots all game but still had only managed a 12-0 lead in a tight game when linebacker Derick Hall made the play that would open the way for Seattle to claim its second title.

item.title: Super Bowl MVP: Kenneth Walker III becomes 1st RB named most valuable of title game in 28 years
item.description: Kenneth Walker III capped a prolific postseason with another big performance on the ground to help the Seattle Seahawks beat the New England Patriots 29-13 for a championship.

item.title: Local Seattle Seahawks fans in 12th Heaven after Super Bowl win
item.description: The 12s turned the volume up to 11.
